newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian wheat fundamentals unchanged.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian wheat fundamentals unchanged.

text.p: The fundamentals of the domestic wheat market remained unchanged this week as concerns about the effect of the El Nino on this year's production continued, the Australian Wheat Board said on Friday.
Prices reflected this with SFE futures trading in the mid $190s per tonne and buyers looking for signs of a break in the weather, it said in its weekly market comment.
This uncertainty should continue for another two to three weeks before the market is able to make more confident predictions about production on the eastern seaboard.
The old crop feedgrain market saw some movement in sorghum values during the week, the AWB said.
A rise in prices reflected the strong international price and continued holding of stocks on-farm with buyers biding higher to encourage grain into the market.
New crop prices remained firm following the lack of significant rainfall in New South Wales to provide relief for growers.
"Continued local dryness will ensure we won't see an easing of prices and in canola this is being supported by dry conditions in Canada impacting on international prices."
Latest Week Year to Date Previous Year

A quiet week of shipping along the eastern sea board with no movement of grain from Victoria, Queensland or South Australia. However, reasonable tonnage was shipped to Pakistan from New South Wales, the AWB said.
Western Australia also moved a number of deliveries to Japan, Malaysia, South Korea and Vietnam.
